subfamily: gin Old-Fashioned, built over ice, after the Codex root (p. 2: spirit, sugar, bitters and water as ice; orthodoxy p. 6)
glass: plain kitchen tumbler (about 250 ml), three or four ordinary ice cubes from the freezer tray
version: v1 (Tomás, round 4, 2026-10-01). Drink unchanged from v0; gin re-keyed to Tanqueray London Dry at 41.3%, the UK bottling (Hester T3: Difford's, Tanners); 47.3% US (retailer). Any juniper-led London dry gin, 40-47.3%; 50 ml at 47% or stronger. Spark: liquorice root syrup; liquorice is purportedly one of Tanqueray's four botanicals, and Oxford hears 'just a hint of licorice' in its finish (TANQUERAY GORDON & CO. pdf 1986). balance.py: 41.3% 28.7%/7.00 g; 40% 27.8%; 47.3% 32.8% edge, 50 ml 31.9%/8.14 g. Sugar held under Arnold's ~7.6 g (LI p. 125) because glycyrrhizin reads sweeter than its grams (unsourced). Liquorice root classed nuts on the safe side: a legume (Oxford pdf 1673), the plant family of peanut; the pour leaves veto-free.
